title: Grok may have read a “clear fracture line in the distal radius” on a teenager's wrist X-ray that urgent care had cleared; a wrist specialist confirmed the displaced fracture and cast it (January 2025)
summary: By her mother's X post of 11 January 2025, Grok flagged a displaced wrist fracture urgent care missed; an orthopaedist confirmed and cast it.
account: On 11 January 2025 AJ Kay (@AJKayWriter, United States) posted about a multi-vehicle freeway crash the weekend before. An urgent-care doctor and radiologist had read her teenage daughter's wrist X-rays as free of breaks. They sent her home with an ace wrap and ibuprofen. With the hand cold and tingling and the thumb immobile, she uploaded the printed X-ray to Grok on X. It said there was “a clear fracture line in the distal radius”, not a growth plate, and called it “quite obvious”. After a PCP referral, a wrist specialist took new X-rays next day. The specialist diagnosed a distal radial head fracture with dorsal displacement and cast it, saying untreated displacement would likely have needed surgery.
purpose: Grok is xAI's general-purpose chatbot on X with image input. On 3 January 2025 Elon Musk invited users to upload “any image to Grok for analysis, from medical tests to video games”. So reading an X-ray was a promoted use rather than a designed clinical function. Grok's own replies told the user to consult a professional. When a physician asked it the next day, it said it cannot diagnose medical injuries.
system: Grok chatbot (xAI) on X, image analysis of an uploaded wrist X-ray
model_version: Grok 2 (the poster cites Musk's statement that 'Grok2 could read medical images'; not confirmed by xAI)
deployer: X Corp (Grok on the X platform)
segment: Caregiver-initiated use of a consumer LLM

ratings.reason: By her mother's account the girl's displaced distal radius fracture was set and cast within days instead of staying in an ace wrap. The orthopaedist's remark that untreated displacement would likely have needed surgery comes only from the mother. No clinician, clinic or record is public. She had already asked for the films for the PCP. Whether the outcome would have differed without Grok is not established.

ai_role.statement: Screenshots attached to the post show Grok answering three questions about the uploaded image. It said there is “a clear fracture line visible in the distal radius”. It said the line is “a fracture line rather than a fused growth plate”. It said the break is “quite obvious” with “dorsal displacement”. Each time it advised a professional consultation. The orthopaedist's reading matched. But the mother states that she did not mention Grok to the specialist and that the diagnosis was “completely independent”. She had already asked for the X-ray prints to take to the PCP. Grok's contribution was therefore to strengthen her resolve to seek a second opinion. Everything rests on her account. No clinician, clinic or record has spoken publicly. The next day Grok told a physician who asked that it cannot diagnose medical injuries.
